page.text2: Discover our sturgeon caviar and trout roe. Learn where they come from, choose a size and order delivery across Ukraine.
about.paragraph2: From the water in which the fish is raised to the temperature during delivery, every detail matters. We handle everything so you can savor the taste of our caviar.
about.alt1: Mum (technologist) with caviar, smile, warm light
about.paragraph3: Our caviar comes from fish farms in the Zakarpattia, Volyn and Chernivtsi regions of Ukraine. Away from major cities and industrial areas, the fish are raised in clean, flowing water that helps shape the caviar’s natural flavour.
about.alt2: Sturgeon farm pools against the hills
about.alt3: Fish farmers working with sturgeon in a farm pool
about.alt4: A hand serving caviar on a spoon
about.paragraph4: Our story began with the domestication of the Azov population of Russian Sturgeon. Our original breeding fish were legally collected from the Sea of Azov to help restore a rare species. Our fish farmers have experience at every stage, from breeding and raising fish to salting caviar. This experience helps us adapt our approach to the characteristics of each batch.
about.paragraph5: We salt the caviar from each sturgeon separately, taking into account the size and density of the grain, and never mix it with other batches. Careful handwork keeps the grains intact, and we use no added flavourings to preserve the caviar’s natural taste.
about.paragraph6: We produce caviar at our own fish processing facility in the Vinnytsia region, registered by the State Service of Ukraine on Food Safety and Consumer Protection (facility registration number: a-UA-02-29-23-VII-PP). The facility operates a certified HACCP food safety system, with defined procedures at every stage, from receiving the fish to packing the caviar.
about.paragraph7: We maintain the required temperature during storage and ship caviar in insulated boxes with ice packs to preserve its quality during delivery.
article-0.paragraph1: Start with a small portion and take your time. Try the caviar on its own first to appreciate the texture of the grains, the saltiness and the finish.
article-0.paragraph2: Open the jar right before serving. Place it on ice or transfer a portion to a chilled caviar server, making sure no meltwater gets inside. Use a mother-of-pearl, glass or porcelain spoon.
article-0.paragraph3: Want to try it with something? Serve it with avocado, a pancake with whipped cream, blini, egg or a baked potato. Warm accompaniments should be served warm rather than hot. For an elegant presentation, try caviar on a fresh oyster.
article-0.paragraph4: Caviar has long been paired with fine drinks. Brut Champagne or dry white wine brings out the flavours of different types of sturgeon caviar. If you prefer spirits, try ice-cold vodka or tequila.
article-1.paragraph1: We use glass jars so you can see the size and colour of the grains and check that there is no excess liquid or foreign matter inside.
article-1.paragraph2: Caviar is sensitive to temperature, so the right packaging helps protect its quality. Before dispatch we check the jar and its label, protect it from damage and place it in an insulated box with ice packs. This keeps the caviar chilled during delivery with Nova Poshta to any city in Ukraine.
article-1.paragraph3: When you receive the parcel, put the caviar in the fridge straight away. Do not leave it somewhere warm.
article-2.paragraph1: The Russian Sturgeon (Acipenser gueldenstaedtii) is one of the best-known members of the sturgeon family. In the wild it lived in the Black, Azov and Caspian Seas and entered rivers to spawn. Today the wild sturgeon is on the verge of extinction and is listed in the Red Book of Ukraine, so caviar is obtained only from farm-raised fish. An adult Russian Sturgeon usually weighs 12–16 kg. Females reach reproductive maturity at 10–14 years of age. Perhaps this is why its caviar is so highly valued. Russian Sturgeon caviar has medium-sized grains ranging from dark grey to brown, with a balanced flavour and distinct nutty notes. It is considered a classic black caviar.
article-2.paragraph2: Bester is a hybrid of two sturgeon species, created by crossing Beluga (Huso huso) with Sterlet (Acipenser ruthenus). It does not occur naturally in the wild. Its name combines Beluga and Sterlet. The first besters were bred in 1952. Bester inherits rapid growth and a large body size of up to 30 kg from Beluga, and early maturity from Sterlet. Females can produce caviar at 5–9 years of age. These characteristics have made Bester one of the most commonly farmed sturgeons worldwide. It is not released into natural waters because of the risk of genetic contamination of pure wild species. Beluga Hybrid caviar has a tender texture, grains ranging from grey to brown and a nutty finish. It combines characteristics of Sterlet and Beluga caviar.
article-2.paragraph3: The Sterlet (Acipenser ruthenus) is the smallest of the sturgeons. It is a freshwater fish: unlike its relatives, it spends its whole life in rivers, including the Danube and the Dnipro. Wild populations have become rare, so today Sterlet is raised on farms. An adult Sterlet usually weighs 1–2 kg. Females reach reproductive maturity at 5–8 years of age, earlier than many other sturgeons. It thrives in ponds with clean, cool, oxygen-rich flowing water. Sterlet caviar has small, dark grains with a tender texture and a mild flavour. It is often recommended for those trying black caviar for the first time.

blog.paragraph3: Archive video from 2020. During annual grading, each fish receives a “health check”. Specialists weigh and examine every sturgeon to assess its health and readiness to spawn. This helps us select fish for caviar harvesting in spring and care for the stock. The video shows a working day at our farm in 2020 before we lost our fish stock in 2023.

blog.paragraph4: An archive article from 2016 about our company’s history. In the summer of 2016 170,000 Azov sturgeon fry were released into the Kalmius River near Mariupol. In 2015 the breeding fish were evacuated from the Donetsk region to the Kherson region because of the hostilities. They were bred there to produce the young fish. The fry were transported in specialised vehicles with a continuous supply of oxygen to the water. The young sturgeon were expected to swim from the Kalmius into the Sea of Azov and return to their native river years later to spawn. The Azov sturgeon is a rare species listed in the Red Book of Ukraine. We preserve this story as a record of our work to conserve sturgeon.

faq.alt1: Caviar on a mother-of-pearl spoon against dark stone
faq.text2: Which caviar should I try first?
faq.paragraph1: If you’re trying black caviar for the first time we recommend Sterlet for its tender texture and delicate flavour. Beluga Hybrid will appeal to those who enjoy a nutty finish, while Premium is a good choice for those who appreciate large grains and rich flavours. If you prefer red caviar, choose Trout for its lightly salted taste and subtle sweetness.
faq.text3: How is bester different from beluga?
faq.paragraph2: Bester is a hybrid of Beluga and Sterlet. A purebred Beluga starts producing caviar only at 20 years of age. This long maturation period makes its caviar a rare and especially valuable delicacy. Bester inherits Beluga’s tender texture and flavour characteristics, but its caviar is a distinct product that we sell as “Beluga Hybrid caviar”.
faq.paragraph3: Premium is our category of selected sturgeon caviar with large grains measuring 3–3.5 mm, harvested from fish aged 10 years or more. It may include caviar from Siberian Sturgeon, Russian Sturgeon or Beluga Hybrid. Premium is a selection category. The flavour profile varies depending on the fish species.
faq.paragraph4: Yes. Sturgeon caviar contains E200 (sorbic acid), and trout caviar contains E211 (sodium benzoate) and E200. They help extend the product’s shelf life. The full ingredients list is available on each product page and on the label.
faq.paragraph5: Our facility operates a certified HACCP food safety system. Every batch of caviar is tested in an accredited laboratory of the State Service of Ukraine on Food Safety and Consumer Protection.
faq.text7: How should I store an unopened jar?
faq.paragraph6: Store sturgeon caviar at −4 °C to −2 °C for up to 12 months and trout caviar at −2 °C to +2 °C for up to 45 days from the date of production. Always follow the shelf life and storage instructions on the label. For sturgeon caviar, choose the coldest section of the fridge and check that the temperature is within the required range. If your fridge is warmer, contact us for advice on how long the caviar can be stored at that temperature.
faq.text8: How long does caviar keep after opening?
faq.paragraph7: No longer than 48 hours: sturgeon caviar at 0 °C to +6 °C and trout caviar at 0 °C to +4 °C. Close the jar tightly and always use a clean spoon.
faq.text9: How should caviar be served and what goes best with it?
faq.paragraph8: Serve it chilled: the jar or caviar server can be placed on ice, making sure no meltwater gets inside. Use a mother-of-pearl, glass or porcelain spoon. Taste black caviar on its own first to appreciate its flavour and texture. Then try it with blini, toast with butter, egg or avocado. Trout caviar pairs well with rye bread, cream cheese and baked potato. Pair with dry white wine, brut Champagne or alcohol-free sparkling wine.

history.paragraph1: In 2015 Ukrainian Caviar Berry started as a full-cycle sturgeon farm and received official state status as a breeding centre for Russian Sturgeon and Beluga.
history.paragraph2: We raised fish from larvae to mature breeding fish and developed a purebred line of the Azov population of Russian Sturgeon. Later, we built our own caviar production facility and implemented a HACCP food safety system.
history.paragraph3: In 2023 we lost all our breeding stock and sturgeon fry. It was the most devastating loss in the farm’s history. We chose to continue the work our fish farmers have devoted more than 20 years too.
history.heading2: A new stage. The same principles.
history.paragraph4: Today, we work with sturgeon and trout farms in the Zakarpattia, Volyn and Chernivtsi regions of Ukraine. We choose partners who raise fish in open water supplied by natural mountain springs and share our commitment to quality.
history.paragraph5: During the spawning season, selected sturgeon are transported alive to our facility in the Vinnytsia region. We collect the caviar using a method known as “milking”, which allows the fish to remain alive after collection. Each batch is salted by hand and prepared for packing.
history.paragraph6: “The way we work has changed, but our principles remain: care for the fish, attention to every batch and the natural taste of caviar for your special moments.”
